claim: A protein trap library made with the gene-break transposon (GBT) in zebrafish (Danio rerio) was generated that could be used to facilitate novel functional genome annotation towards understanding molecular underpinnings of human diseases.
source: Previously we showed the generation of a protein trap library made with the gene-break transposon (GBT) in zebrafish (Danio rerio) that could be used to facilitate novel functional genome annotation towards understanding molecular underpinnings of human diseases (Ichino et al, 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ichino et al, 2020, indicating prior published work.

claim: SSS is a group of heart rhythm disorders caused by malfunction of the sinus node, the heart's primary pacemaker.
source: SSS is a group of heart rhythm disorders caused by malfunction of the sinus node, the heart's primary pacemaker.
evidence: This is a definitional statement based on established medical knowledge about sick sinus syndrome.

claim: Molecular mechanisms of SSS remain difficult to decipher partially owing to its aging-associated phenotypic manifestation and low expressivity.
source: Partially owing to its aging-associated phenotypic manifestation and low expressivity, molecular mechanisms of SSS remain difficult to decipher.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the challenges in studying age-related diseases with variable penetrance.

claim: From 609 GBT lines screened, a collection of 35 zebrafish insertional cardiac (ZIC) mutants was generated in which each mutant traps a gene with cardiac expression.
source: From 609 GBT lines screened, we generated a collection of 35 zebrafish insertional cardiac (ZIC) mutants in which each mutant traps a gene with cardiac expression.
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental data from the screening process.

claim: Three GBT mutants with SSS-like phenotypes were identified from electrocardiographic measurements of 35 ZIC lines.
source: We further employed electrocardiographic measurements to screen these 35 ZIC lines and identified three GBT mutants with SSS-like phenotypes.
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental findings from ECG screening.

claim: Dnajb6 is a novel SSS causative gene.
source: More detailed functional studies on one of the arrhythmogenic mutants, GBT411, in both zebrafish and mouse models unveiled Dnajb6 as a novel SSS causative gene with a unique expression pattern within the subpopulation of sinus node pacemaker cells that partially overlaps with the expression of hyperpolarization activated cyclic nucleotide gated channel 4 (HCN4), supporting heterogeneity of the cardiac pacemaker cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by functional studies in zebrafish and mouse models as described in the manuscript.

claim: Dnajb6 has a unique expression pattern within the subpopulation of sinus node pacemaker cells that partially overlaps with the expression of HCN4.
source: More detailed functional studies on one of the arrhythmogenic mutants, GBT411, in both zebrafish and mouse models unveiled Dnajb6 as a novel SSS causative gene with a unique expression pattern within the subpopulation of sinus node pacemaker cells that partially overlaps with the expression of hyperpolarization activated cyclic nucleotide gated channel 4 (HCN4), supporting heterogeneity of the cardiac pacemaker cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data showing partial colocalization of DNAJB6 with HCN4.

claim: The expression pattern of Dnajb6 supports heterogeneity of the cardiac pacemaker cells.
source: More detailed functional studies on one of the arrhythmogenic mutants, GBT411, in both zebrafish and mouse models unveiled Dnajb6 as a novel SSS causative gene with a unique expression pattern within the subpopulation of sinus node pacemaker cells that partially overlaps with the expression of hyperpolarization activated cyclic nucleotide gated channel 4 (HCN4), supporting heterogeneity of the cardiac pacemaker cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the partial overlap of DNAJB6 with HCN4 expression.

claim: Cardiac arrhythmia affects >2% of individuals in community-dwelling adults.
source: Cardiac arrhythmia affects >2% of individuals in community-dwelling adults (Khurshid et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Khurshid et al., 2018.

claim: SSS manifests a spectrum of presentations such as sinus pause or arrest (SA), bradycardia, sinoatrial exit block, or tachy-brady syndrome accompanied by atrial fibrillation (AF).
source: SSS manifests a spectrum of presentations such as sinus pause or arrest (SA), bradycardia, sinoatrial exit block, or tachy-brady syndrome accompanied by atrial fibrillation (AF) (Semelka et al., 2013; De Ponti et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Semelka et al., 2013 and De Ponti et al., 2018.

claim: 20% to 60% SSS patients show abnormal response to autonomic stresses.
source: In addition, 20% to 60% SSS patients show abnormal response to autonomic stresses (Dakkak and Doukky, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dakkak and Doukky, 2020.

claim: SSS occurs most commonly in elderly, with an estimated prevalence of 1 case per 600 adults over age 65.
source: SSS occurs most commonly in elderly, with an estimated prevalence of 1 case per 600 adults over age 65 (Dobrzynski et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dobrzynski et al., 2007.

claim: SSS is the most common indication for pacemaker implantation worldwide.
source: While SSS is the most common indication for pacemaker implantation worldwide (Mond and Proclemer, 2011), the mechanisms of SSS remain poorly understood, making it difficult to stratify SSS risk in vulnerable cohorts of patients and development of effective pharmacologic therapy for pacemaker abnormalities.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mond and Proclemer, 2011.

claim: The mechanisms of SSS remain poorly understood.
source: While SSS is the most common indication for pacemaker implantation worldwide (Mond and Proclemer, 2011), the mechanisms of SSS remain poorly understood, making it difficult to stratify SSS risk in vulnerable cohorts of patients and development of effective pharmacologic therapy for pacemaker abnormalities.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Mutations in SCN5A have been found to cause SSS.
source: While mutations in the cardiac sodium channel α-subunit encoding gene (SCN5A) (Nof et al., 2007; Tan et al., 2001) and hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-aged channel encoding gene (HCN4) Schulze-Bahr et al., 2003; Verkerk and Wilders, 2015 have been found to cause SSS, only a few other genes affecting the structure and/or function of the SAN were identified to increase the risk of developing SSS (Anderson and Benson, 2010; Holm et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nof et al., 2007 and Tan et al., 2001.

claim: Mutations in HCN4 have been found to cause SSS.
source: While mutations in the cardiac sodium channel α-subunit encoding gene (SCN5A) (Nof et al., 2007; Tan et al., 2001) and hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-aged channel encoding gene (HCN4) Schulze-Bahr et al., 2003; Verkerk and Wilders, 2015 have been found to cause SSS, only a few other genes affecting the structure and/or function of the SAN were identified to increase the risk of developing SSS (Anderson and Benson, 2010; Holm et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Schulze-Bahr et al., 2003 and Verkerk and Wilders, 2015.

claim: Only a few genes affecting the structure and/or function of the SAN were identified to increase the risk of developing SSS.
source: While mutations in the cardiac sodium channel α-subunit encoding gene (SCN5A) (Nof et al., 2007; Tan et al., 2001) and hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-aged channel encoding gene (HCN4) Schulze-Bahr et al., 2003; Verkerk and Wilders, 2015 have been found to cause SSS, only a few other genes affecting the structure and/or function of the SAN were identified to increase the risk of developing SSS (Anderson and Benson, 2010; Holm et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Anderson and Benson, 2010 and Holm et al., 2011.

claim: Classic human genetic linkage analysis-based approach is largely limited by the availability of suitable pedigree, especially in age-dependent diseases.
source: Classic human genetic linkage analysis-based approach has played important roles in gene discovery, but it is largely limited by the availability of suitable pedigree, especially in this age-dependent disease (Zhu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhu et al., 2018.

claim: Genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have been used to identify novel genetic susceptibility factors associated with SSS.
source: More recently, the genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have been used to identify novel genetic susceptibility factors associated with SSS (Holm et al., 2011; Monfredi and Boyett, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Holm et al., 2011 and Monfredi and Boyett, 2015.

claim: It has been difficult to confidently establish genotype-phenotype relationships for the vast amount of variants identified by GWAS owing to its statistic and associative nature.
source: However, owing to its statistic and associative nature, it has been difficult to confidently establish genotype-phenotype relationships for the vast amount of variants (Lin and Musunuru, 2018; Tam et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lin and Musunuru, 2018 and Tam et al., 2019.

claim: A zebrafish heart has conserved myocardium, endocardium, and epicardium as found in human.
source: Despite its small body size, a zebrafish heart has conserved myocardium, endocardium, and epicardium as found in human, and adult zebrafish shows strikingly similar cardiac physiology to humans (Bakkers, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bakkers, 2011.

claim: Adult zebrafish shows strikingly similar cardiac physiology to humans.
source: Despite its small body size, a zebrafish heart has conserved myocardium, endocardium, and epicardium as found in human, and adult zebrafish shows strikingly similar cardiac physiology to humans (Bakkers, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bakkers, 2011.

claim: Adult zebrafish heart rate is around 100 beats per minute (bpm).
source: Its heart rate is around 100 beats per minute (bpm), which is much comparable to that in human than in rodents.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about zebrafish cardiac physiology.

claim: Adult zebrafish models for human cardiac diseases such as cardiomyopathies have been successfully generated.
source: Adult zebrafish models for human cardiac diseases such as cardiomyopathies have been successfully generated (Ding et al., 2020a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ding et al., 2020a.

claim: The GBT-based gene-trap system in zebrafish enables disruption of gene function reversibly at high efficiency (>99% at the RNA level).
source: Our team recently reported a gene-breaking transposon (GBT)-based gene-trap system in zebrafish which enables to disrupt gene function reversibly at high efficiency (>99% at the RNA level) (Clark et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Clark et al., 2011.

claim: Approximately 1,200 GBT lines have been generated.
source: Approximately 1,200 GBT lines have been generated, laying a foundation for adult phenotype-based forward genetic screens (Ichino et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ichino et al., 2020.

claim: Novel genetic factors of doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy (DIC), such as dnajb6b, sorbs2b and rxraa, were successfully identified through stressing the ZIC collection with doxorubicin.
source: Through stressing the ZIC collection with doxorubicin, an anti-cancer drug, we demonstrated that novel genetic factors of doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy (DIC), such as Dnaj (Hsp40) homology, subfamily B, member 6b (dnajb6b), sorbin and SH3 domain-containing 2b (sorbs2b) and retinoid x receptor alpha a (rxraa), could be successfully identified (Ding et al., 2016; Ding et al., 2020b; Ma et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ding et al., 2016, Ding et al., 2020b, and Ma et al., 2020.

claim: The baseline frequency of aging-associated SSS in wild-type (WT) adult zebrafish aged around 2 years old is about 1 out of 20 fish (5%).
source: As reported recently, in WT fish aged around 2 years old, we noted baseline SA episodes in about 1 out of 20 fish (5%) fish Yan et al., 2020.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Yan et al., 2020.

claim: 44 GBT mutants with either embryonic or adult heart expression were identified from screening 609 GBT lines based on their mRFP expression.
source: We screened 609 GBT lines based on their mRFP expression and identified 44 mutants with either the embryonic or adult heart expression Ding et al., 2016.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ding et al., 2016.

claim: 35 mutants with a single copy of the GBT insertion were identified after 2–4 generations of outcross.
source: Then, we outcrossed these 44 lines, aided by Southern blotting to identify offsprings with a lower copy number of insertions, Ding et al., 2013 and identified 35 mutants with a single copy of the GBT insertion after 2–4 generations of outcross (Table 1; Ding et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ding et al., 2013 and Ding et al., 2016.

claim: The genetic loci of GBT inserts in the 35 mutants were mapped using a combination of inverse PCR and/or 5'- and 3'-RACE PCR cloning approaches.
source: Using a combination of inverse PCR and/or 5'- and 3'-RACE PCR cloning approaches, we mapped the genetic loci of GBT inserts in these 35 mutants (Table 1; Ding et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ding et al., 2013 and reference to Table 1.

claim: Most of the affected genes in the 35 ZIC mutants have human orthologs with a corresponding Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) number.
source: Most of the affected genes have human orthologs with a corresponding Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) number.
evidence: This is supported by the data presented in Table 1 showing OMIM numbers for most genes.

claim: Significantly increased SA incidence was noted in all three homozygous mutants (GBT103/cyth3a, GBT410/vapal, and GBT411/dnajb6b) at 16 months of age compared to WT fish.
source: In contrast to 5% WT fish whereby SA episodes can be detected, significantly increased SA incidence was noted in all three homozygous mutants at 16 months of age, with an incidence of 57.1% in the GBT103/cyth3a, 44.4% in the GBT410/vapal, and 40% in the GBT411/dnajb6b homozygous mutants, respectively (Table 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 2.

claim: A reduced heart rate was noted in the GBT411/dnajb6b homozygous mutants but not in the other two GBT homozygous mutants.
source: In addition, we also noted a reduced heart rate, another SSS phenotypic trait in the GBT411/dnajb6b, but not the other two GBT homozygous mutants (Table 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 2.

claim: GBT411-/- fish showed increased RR interval, which is consistent with reduced heart rate.
source: Detailed analysis of ECG indices showed increased RR interval in the GBT411/dnajb6b homozygous mutants (GBT411-/-) (Supplementary file 2), which is consistent with reduced heart rate.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data referenced in Supplementary file 2.

claim: GBT411-/- fish manifested aberrant heart rate response to both atropine and carbachol, while its response to isoproterenol appeared to be similar to that in WT control animals.
source: After administrating these drugs to the GBT411-/- fish at 1 year old via intraperitoneal (IP) injection, we noted aberrant heart rate response to both atropine and carbachol, while its response to isoproterenol appeared to be similar to that in WT control animals (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: SA incidence was significantly increased in the GBT411-/- fish at 10 months of age after verapamil stress.
source: Next, we stressed the GBT411-/- fish with verapamil, an L-type Ca2+ channel antagonists, to stress out cardiac pacemaking and unmask SSS phenotype. Indeed, SA incidence was significantly increased in the GBT411-/- fish at 10 months of age (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data referenced in Supplementary file 1.

claim: The heart rate was significantly reduced in the GBT411-/- fish compared to WT controls after verapamil stress.
source: Similarly, the heart rate was significantly reduced in the GBT411-/- fish compared to WT controls.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from verapamil stress experiments.

claim: Dnajb6b was previously identified as a cardiomyopathy-associated gene, disruption of which led to abnormal cardiac remodeling in zebrafish.
source: Dnajb6b was previously identified as a cardiomyopathy-associated gene, disruption of which led to abnormal cardiac remodeling in zebrafish, Ding et al., 2016 raising concerns on whether the arrhythmic phenotype in the GBT411/dnajb6b mutant is a primary defect in the cardiac conduction system or a consequence of cardiac remodeling in cardiomyocytes.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ding et al., 2016.

claim: The mRFP positive, Dnajb6b-expressing cells partially overlap with the EGFP signal labeling both AVC and SAN cells at the base of atrium in the embryonic heart at 3 days post-fertilization.
source: Co-localization analysis demonstrated that the mRFP positive, Dnajb6b-expressing cells partially overlap with the EGFP signal labeling both AVC and SAN cells at the base of atrium in the embryonic heart at 3 days post-fertilization (Figure 2A-C).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-localization analysis data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: In the GBT411/dnajb6b homozygous (GBT411-/-) adult hearts crossed with the sqET33-mi59B line, EGFP signal in the AVC region appeared to be more diffused compared to that in GBT411+/-.
source: However, in the GBT411/dnajb6b homozygous (GBT411-/-) adult hearts crossed with the sqET33-mi59B line, EGFP signal in the AVC region appeared to be more diffused compared to that in GBT411+/-, while no EGFP-positive SAN cells was detected in 3 out of 9 fish hearts examined (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G and H.

claim: No EGFP-positive SAN cells was detected in 3 out of 9 GBT411-/- fish hearts examined.
source: However, in the GBT411/dnajb6b homozygous (GBT411-/-) adult hearts crossed with the sqET33-mi59B line, EGFP signal in the AVC region appeared to be more diffused compared to that in GBT411+/-, while no EGFP-positive SAN cells was detected in 3 out of 9 fish hearts examined (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G and H.

claim: The mouse DNAJB6 protein can be detected in all four cardiac chambers in a sectioned mouse heart tissue.
source: The mouse DNAJB6 protein can be detected in all four cardiac chambers in a sectioned mouse heart tissue (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: A highly enriched expression of DNAJB6 was found in the SAN region, as defined by the expression of HCN4 channels.
source: Interestingly, we found a highly enriched expression of DNAJB6 in the SAN region, as defined by the expression of HCN4 channels which are responsible for the generation of hyperpolarization-activated pacemaker 'funny' current in pacemaker cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Only a proportion of DNAJB6-positive cells showed colocalization with the HCN4-positive cells.
source: However, at higher magnification images, only a proportion of DNAJB6-positive cells showed colocalization with the HCN4-positive cells (arrows for colocalized cells vs. stars for non-colocalized cells in Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Co-localization of DNAJB6 with TBX3 was noted.
source: In addition, co-localization of DNAJB6 with TBX3, a transcription factor that specifies the formation of the SAN cells, was noted (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: A negative correlation between DNAJB6 and TBX3 signal intensity was appreciated: cells with strong DNAJB6 expression tend to overlap with cells that show weak TBX3 signal, while cells with weak DNAJB6 expression tend to overlap with the cells with strong TBX3 signal.
source: More interestingly, a negative correlation between DNAJB6 and TBX3 signal intensity was appreciated: cells with strong DNAJB6 expression tend to overlap with cells that show weak TBX3 signal, while cells with weak DNAJB6 expression tend to overlap with the cells with strong TBX3 signal (Figure 3C-E).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 3C-E.

claim: The overall TBX3 signal in the SAN tissue of DNAJB6 heterozygous knock out (KO) mouse was significantly increased compared to that in WT control.
source: Furthermore, the overall TBX3 signal in the SAN tissue of DNAJB6 heterozygous knock out (KO) mouse (see below) was significantly increased compared to that in WT control (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining and quantification data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The Dnajb6 mutant mouse harbors a deletion of 36,843 bp nucleotides spanning from the first intron to the last intron of Dnajb6 gene located in the Chromosome 5.
source: The mutant harbors a deletion of 36,843 bp nucleotides spanning from the first intron to the last intron of Dnajb6 gene located in the Chromosome 5, which was created by the insertion of the Velocigene ZEN-Ub1 cassette and subsequent LoxP excision using Cre (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the description of the knockout mouse generation shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Both the DNAJB6 short (S) and long (L) isoforms were reduced by ~50% in Dnajb6+/- mouse embryonic hearts at E12.5 stage.
source: At the protein level, both the DNAJB6 short (S) and long (L) isoforms were reduced by ~50% in Dnajb6+/- mouse embryonic hearts at E12.5 stage (+/-), and near completely depleted in Dnajb6-/- mutant hearts.
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blotting data.

claim: DNAJB6 short (S) and long (L) isoforms were near completely depleted in Dnajb6-/- mutant hearts.
source: At the protein level, both the DNAJB6 short (S) and long (L) isoforms were reduced by ~50% in Dnajb6+/- mouse embryonic hearts at E12.5 stage (+/-), and near completely depleted in Dnajb6-/- mutant hearts.
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blotting data.

claim: Dnajb6-/- KO mice were embryonic lethal, died in the uterus at about E13.5 stage, likely due to the placental defects.
source: Consistent with a previous report, Hunter et al., 1999 Dnajb6-/- KO mice were embryonic lethal, died in the uterus at about E13.5 stage, likely due to the placental defects (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hunter et al., 1999 and experimental observation.

claim: The Dnajb6 +/- mice were able to grow to adulthood without visually noticeable phenotypes until at least 1 year of age.
source: The Dnajb6 +/- mice were able to grow to adulthood without visually noticeable phenotypes until at least 1 year of age.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the study.

claim: Cardiac mechanical function remained normal in Dnajb6+/- mice, as indicated by indistinguishable cardiac echocardiography indices from those of WT siblings at the same age.
source: Cardiac mechanical function remained normal, as indicated by indistinguishable cardiac echocardiography indices from those of WT siblings at the same age (Table 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by echocardiography data presented in Table 3.

claim: No abnormal myocardial structural morphology was detected in the left ventricle (LV) of Dnajb6+/- mice.
source: No abnormal myocardial structural morphology was detected in the left ventricle (LV) of Dnajb6+/- mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by histology data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Increased frequency of SA and AVB episodes, as well as bradycardia phenotype, were noted in Dnajb6+/- mice at 6 months old.
source: However, increased frequency of SA and AVB episodes, as well as bradycardia phenotype, were noted in Dnajb6+/- mice at 6 months old (Figure 4D and E, and Table 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by ECG data shown in Figure 4D and E, and Table 4.

claim: The Dnajb6+/- mice exhibited an impaired response to autonomic stimuli including isoproterenol and carbachol.
source: Similar to the GBT411/dnajb6b mutant in zebrafish, the Dnajb6+/- mice exhibited an impaired response to autonomic stimuli including isoproterenol and carbachol (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Dnajb6+/- mice manifest SSS phenotype without structural/functional remodeling of the heart.
source: Together, these studies suggest that Dnajb6+/- mice manifest SSS phenotype without structural/functional remodeling of the heart.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combination of ECG and echocardiography data.

claim: Significant increase in the number of leading pacemakers located outside of the SAN, including the subsidiary atrial pacemakers and inter-atrial septum pacemakers, was observed in Dnajb6+/- mice.
source: In contrast, significant increase in the number of leading pacemakers located outside of the SAN, including the subsidiary atrial pacemakers and inter-atrial septum pacemakers, was observed in Dnajb6+/- mice (p=0.039 vs. WT mice).
evidence: This claim is supported by optical mapping data.

claim: In Dnajb6+/- mice, a highly irregular heart rate was found, accompanied by the presence of multiple competing pacemakers and a beat-to-beat migration of the leading pacemaker between various sites which included SAN, right atrial ectopic (subsidiary) pacemakers, and inter-atrial septum.
source: In addition, in Dnajb6+/- mice, we also found a highly irregular heart rate, accompanied by the presence of multiple competing pacemakers and a beat-to-beat migration of the leading pacemaker between various sites which included SAN, right atrial ectopic (subsidiary) pacemakers, and inter-atrial septum (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by optical mapping data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Bradycardia phenotype was consistently detected in the isolated atrial preparations from Dnajb6+/- mice.
source: Similar to the results from the in vivo studies, bradycardia phenotype was consistently detected in the isolated atrial preparations as well (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by optical mapping data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Optical mapping on isolated atrial preparations revealed different responses of heart rate during isoproterenol, atropine, and carbachol stimulations in Dnajb6+/- mice.
source: Optical mapping on isolated atrial preparations further revealed different responses of heart rate during isoproterenol, atropine, and carbachol stimulations in Dnajb6+/- mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by optical mapping data.

claim: Significantly increased cycle length (CL) variations were observed at baseline and upon carbachol stimulation in Dnajb6+/- mice.
source: Significantly increased cycle length (CL) variations were also observed at baseline and upon carbachol stimulation (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by optical mapping data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: In Dnajb6+/- mice, significant prolongation of the SAN recovery time corrected to beating rate (cSANRT) was found measured both at baseline and under autonomic stresses, including stimulation by isoproterenol, carbachol, and atropine.
source: Furthermore, in Dnajb6+/- mice, we found significant prolongation of the SAN recovery time corrected to beating rate (cSANRT) measured both at baseline and under autonomic stresses, including stimulation by isoproterenol, carbachol, and atropine (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), confirming the presence of SAN dysfunction in Dnajb6+/- mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by optical mapping data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The first spontaneous post-pacing atrial beats during SANRT measurements in Dnajb6+/- mice were originated from ectopic locations outside of the SAN.
source: Optical mapping also showed that, unlike WT, the first spontaneous post-pacing atrial beats during SANRT measurements in Dnajb6+/- mice were originated from ectopic locations outside of the SAN (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B), further supporting a suppressed SAN function.
evidence: This claim is supported by optical mapping data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: Histological evaluation of fibrosis tissue content in Dnajb6+/- mouse atria did not reveal any significant difference compared to WT mice, for both atria and SAN.
source: Histological evaluation of fibrosis tissue content in Dnajb6+/- mouse atria, however, did not reveal any significant difference compared to WT mice, for both atria and SAN.
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis data.

claim: A subpopulation of computational model variants (n=438) displayed a slower firing rate at baseline, an increased response to isoproterenol, and a decreased response to carbachol administration, thus recapitulating the Dnajb6+/- mice phenotype.
source: Nevertheless, the cell-cell variability in heart rate response allowed identifying two subpopulations of model variants, whereby several models (n=438) displayed a slower firing rate at baseline, an increased response to isoproterenol, and a decreased response to carbachol administration (Figure 6C and D), thus recapitulating the Dnajb6+/- mice as measured in our ex vivo functional experiments (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational modeling data shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: The analysis of computational models revealed a significant decrease in the maximal conductance of the fast (Nav1.5) Na+ current, the L-type Ca2+ current (ICa,L), the transient outward, sustained, and acetylcholine-activated K+ currents, the background Na+ and Ca2+ currents, as well as the ryanodine receptor maximal release flux of the Dnajb6+/- vs. WT model variants.
source: The analysis revealed a significant decrease in the maximal conductance of the fast (Nav1.5) Na+ current, the L-type Ca2+ current (ICa,L), the transient outward, sustained, and acetylcholine-activated K+ currents, the background Na+ and Ca2+ currents, as well as the ryanodine receptor maximal release flux of the Dnajb6+/- vs. WT model variants.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational modeling analysis.

claim: The analysis of computational models revealed a significant increase in the Na+/Ca2+-exchanger maximal transport rate, and conductance of the T-type Ca2+ current and the slowly-activating delayed rectifier K+ current in Dnajb6+/- vs. WT model variants.
source: We also found a significant increase in the Na+/Ca2+-exchanger maximal transport rate, and conductance of the T-type Ca2+ current and the slowly-activating delayed rectifier K+ current.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational modeling analysis.

claim: 107 differentially expressed (DE) genes were identified in Dnajb6+/- mice right atrial tissues compared with WT controls, among which 37 genes were upregulated and 70 genes were downregulated.
source: Based on a cut-off of adjusted p-value <0.05 and≥2 folds change, 107 differentially expressed (DE) genes were identified, among which 37 genes were upregulated and 70 genes were downregulated in the Dnajb6+/- mice compared with WT controls (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-sequencing data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: Calcium handling related protein-encoding genes like Slc24a2 and Cdh20, ion channel-encoding genes including Slc9a3r1, Kcnh7, Fxyd5, and Gjb5, as well as 4 Wnt pathway related genes were differentially expressed in the Dnajb6+/- mice.
source: Among these 107 differentially expressed genes, we noted calcium handling related protein-encoding genes like Slc24a2 and Cdh20, ion channel-encoding genes including Slc9a3r1, Kcnh7, Fxyd5, and Gjb5 (Figure 7A), as well as 4 Wnt pathway related genes (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-sequencing data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Quantitative RT-PCR analysis experimentally confirmed dysregulation of calcium handling, ion channel-encoding, and Wnt pathway related genes in the Dnajb6+/- mice.
source: We then performed quantitative RT-PCR analysis and experimentally confirmed dysregulation of these genes in the Dnajb6+/- mice (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Out of 313 variants with minor allele frequency ≥1% in DNAJB6, four variants showed nominal association (p<0.05) with SSS in a GWAS dataset.
source: Out of 313 variants with minor allele frequency ≥1% in DNAJB6, four variants showed nominal association (p<0.05, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of GWAS data.

claim: The most significant variant associated with SSS was observed for rs754941044 (p=0.0193), which was predicted as a splice acceptor variant.
